metaData.originalTitle: Fable 5 禁令始末：Anthropic 亲手写下的剧本，反过来演了它自己
metaData.title: The Fable 5 Ban: The Script Anthropic Wrote, Turned Against Itself
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth review of the US government's export control ban on Anthropic's flagship model, Fable 5, revealing the underlying technical disputes, political games, and deep irony, while exploring the core issue of power checks and balances in AI governance.
metaData.summary: Starting with the US Department of Commerce's export control ban on Anthropic's flagship models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, on June 12, 2026, the article details the full scope of the event. The trigger was a security test report submitted to the government by Amazon, claiming the model could be jailbroken for cyberattacks. However, Anthropic and several independent security researchers argued that the jailbreak was 'narrow and non-general,' far from constituting a national security threat. The article further reveals the underlying political grievances: Anthropic's relationship with the Trump administration had been strained due to its refusal of Pentagon contract terms and being labeled a 'supply chain risk.' The deepest irony lies in the fact that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei had previously written an article advocating for the government's right to prevent or withdraw the deployment of high-risk models. Yet, when the government actually exercised this power, it lacked the transparent procedures and checks and balances he had argued for. The article ultimately leads the discussion to the core dilemma of AI governance: who has the right to shut down the 'genius nation in the data center,' and by what rules should this power be exercised.

mainPoints.point: The Fable 5 ban is the most aggressive action the US government has ever taken against a single AI model.
mainPoints.explanation: The Commerce Department, citing export controls, suspended all foreign nationals' access to the model, including Anthropic's own foreign employees, forcing the company to shut down its flagship model globally.

mainPoints.point: The core of the technical dispute lies in a fundamental disagreement over the severity of the 'jailbreak.'
mainPoints.explanation: Amazon's report claimed the model could be used for cyberattacks, but Anthropic and independent security researchers argued the jailbreak was 'narrow and non-general,' far from a national security threat, and that other publicly available models could achieve the same.

mainPoints.point: The event is the culmination of long-standing political grievances between Anthropic and the Trump administration.
mainPoints.explanation: From refusing Pentagon contract terms and being labeled a 'supply chain risk' to being excluded from Department of Defense AI procurement, Anthropic's relationship with the government had been tense, and the ban was an eruption of this accumulated resentment.

mainPoints.point: The deepest irony is that Anthropic handed the government the very logic used against it.
mainPoints.explanation: CEO Dario Amodei had previously argued for the government's right to prevent the deployment of high-risk models, but when the government actually used this power, it lacked the transparent procedures and checks he advocated for, leading Anthropic to accuse the government of not following these principles.

mainPoints.point: The incident exposes a vacuum of power checks and balances in AI governance.
mainPoints.explanation: On one hand, a company alone holds the power to reshape the cybersecurity landscape; on the other, the government can shut down a model with a single unexplained letter. Neither side has sufficient checks, presenting the most urgent governance challenge of the AI era.

keyQuotes: If you describe your product as 'weapons-grade' in every press release, the government will eventually take you at your word.
The government should have the right to prevent or withdraw the deployment of a model when it is judged to pose an unacceptable risk.

Who should hold the key to shut down the 'nation of geniuses,' and by what rules should that key be used? This storm didn't provide an answer; it just laid the question bare for everyone to see for the first time.
